content.text: -    Viral URI / rhinosinusitis supportive care: mucolytic (guaifenesin) - w NSAIDs for pain · nasal saline sprays · intranasal glucocorticoids · decongestants
-    Acute bronchitis: cough med (w dextromethorphan · benzonatate · codeine)
-    Viral URI / rhinosinusitis supportive care: PO decongestants (pseudoephedrine) - topical nasal vasoconstrictors (phenylephrine · oxymetazoline)
-    Rhinitis medicamentosa (rebound congestion): major side effect of intranasal phenylephrine, esp used >3 days
-    Common cold: Sxtomatic relief w antihist or decongestants (adults only)
CF: ↑dose ibuprofen ↓lung inflam → slows airway damage & dz progression
-    Hyponatremia w Sx: 100 mL bolus 3% saline, repeat twice more PRN - monitor Na hourly until ↑4–6 mEq/L
-    Edematous hyponatremia: 3% saline 15–30 mL/hr + IV furosemide (≥40 mg) BID - target ↑4–6 mEq/L per 24 hr, stop when Na ≥125
-    Bronchiectasis: nebulized hypertonic saline to clear secretions
CF: airway clearance - give bronchodilator before inhaled hypertonic saline & chest PT
MOA: anti-inflam via multi actions on WBCs
Carpal tunnel syndrome: local inj (or PO)
Plantar fasciitis: inj ⍉1st-line (↑risk of fascia rupture + fat pad atrophy) → short-term only - topical: limited evidence
▪︎OA: intra-articular inj relieves joint pain for several wks - ≤4x/yr per joint
Pericarditis: refractory/recurr only - ⍉routine early (↑recurr) - ⍉after MI (impairs myocard heal)
▪︎Alopecia areata: intralesional corticosteroid (triamcinolone q4–6 wks) - topical corticosteroid (fluocinolone acetonide cream BID)
▪︎Pityriasis rosea: may improve lesions + pruritus but ⍉routine (lack of evidence - relapse concern)
Nasal polyps + allergic rhinitis: short course
Lichen planus: topical or PO steroids (severity-dep)
Aphthous stomatitis: complex/refractory (PO prednisone x4-7 days)
▪︎Bact meningitis: dexamethasone w abx (adjunct) → ↓inflam + prevent neuro comps (ex hearing loss)
▪︎Sarcoidosis: tx of choice (prednisone, up to 6mo b4 taper)
▪︎Berylliosis: Sxtomatic + abnl PFTs (ex, prednisone) - most need lifelong ↓dose
▪︎Primary AI (Addison): lifelong replace (prednisone · hydrocortisone · dexamethasone) + mineralocorticoid (fludrocortisone)
▪︎Cushing dz postop: empiric hydrocortisone for cortisol w.draw Sx - taper slowly
▪︎ITP: life-threatening bleed → IV methylprednisolone - ⍉rapid plt rise needed → PO dexamethasone or prednisone
▪︎GPA: systemic GC + MTX (limited dz) - + cyclophosphamide (more severe dz)
↑bone catabolism or antagonize vit D driven Ca absorb
Stim gastric acid & pepsin prod → take w food
Admin: IV for critically ill · PO · rectal
Bell palsy: 60–80 mg/day x1 wk - ideally start w.in first 3 days of onset
GCA: ↑dose prednisone PO (IV methylprednisolone if vision loss)
SLE: short-term prednisone initially → taper once HCQ or chloroquine takes effect
Admin: IV for critically ill · PO · rectal

: cortisol & other steroid hormones bind intracell receptors - steroid-receptor complex enters nucleus & acts as transcription factor → turn on genes → synth specific proteins responsible for physio actions
↑BG · ↑protein catabolism from musc/bone · antagonist of insulin
Mineralocorticoid effects: salt/H2O retention · potassium loss
•Replace therapy: AI (Addison's dz) and CAH (defects in enzymes for steroid hormone synth)
•Dexamethasone suppression test (DST): dx of Cushing’s syndrome
•Tx of chronic inflam dz: RA · UC · asthma · SLE · eye & skin inflam
•Tx of allergic rxns: drug · serum & transfusion rxns
•IS: prev of graft reject after transplantation
